items.text: While alive supervision is active, when a supervised task has not completed an execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own, the controller shall detect an alive fault (code 1) for that task.
The controller shall start alive supervision when the start-up integrity checks have passed.
When a supervised task starts more than its configured start limit after its release, the controller shall detect a late-start fault (code 2) for that task; the default start limit is 2 ms.

When a supervised task has not completed its execution at the instant its execution time reaches its configured execution limit, the controller shall detect an overrun fault (code 3) for that task at that instant; the default limit is 3 ms for each 10 ms task and 20 ms for T_DIAG.
items.rationale: Single rule: the overrun is detected at limit expiry (CON-SUP-103, CON-SUP-105), so detection never occurs before the limit is reached and never later than expiry. Whether a task completing exactly at the limit instant is an overrun is not decided by the inputs; see OP-SYS-002.

items.text: The controller shall measure task start and execution times with a resolution of 100 µs.
At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle have not arrived in the configured order, the controller shall detect a flow fault (code 4).
When a checkpoint of a 10 ms task (T_IN, T_CTRL or T_OUT) released in a control cycle is missing at the end of that cycle, the controller shall detect a flow fault (code 4).
items.rationale: Scope limited to the 10 ms tasks, whose execution limit (3 ms, CON-SUP-103) lies within the 10 ms cycle. For T_DIAG (execution limit 20 ms, CON-SUP-103) the checkpoint position and the cycle in which it is due are not decided by the inputs; a plausible rule would be invented, so it is recorded as OP-SYS-003.

items.text: The controller shall take the set of supervised tasks, their start limits, execution limits and checkpoint order from configuration data, without a change of supervisor code.

At start-up, when a configuration value is outside its allowed range (a timing limit longer than the task period, a zero period or an unknown task), the controller shall detect a configuration fault (code 9).

While control cycles are running and no alive fault (code 1), late-start fault (code 2), overrun fault (code 3) or flow fault (code 4) has been detected since the last reset, the controller shall refresh the independent watchdog so that the time from the start of the first control cycle to the first refresh and the time between two consecutive refreshes are each less than 100 ms.
items.rationale: Finding F-sys-req-item-r3-001: a positive refresh obligation is added; the 100 ms timeout (CON-SUP-106) bounds the refresh interval, so fault-free operation needs an interval below 100 ms. The exact refresh period or margin is not given by the inputs, see OP-SYS-012. The prohibition after a fault stays in SYS-SUP-043. Earlier finding F-sys-req-item-r2-002: refresh eligibility is defined directly on the detected faults, without attributing a fault to a task. A flow fault (SYS-SUP-006, SYS-SUP-007; CON-SUP-104) is defined for the control cycle, so no per-task health is needed; every detected fault of codes 1 to 4, whichever task or cycle it concerns, stops the refresh. Fault rules: alive (CON-SUP-102), late start and overrun (CON-SUP-103), flow (CON-SUP-104) per SYS-SUP-001, 003, 004, 006, 007. After a fault the recovery path is a reset (CON-SUP-110), so eligibility is evaluated per reset. Finding F-sys-req-set-r1-009: the first refresh after control cycles begin is now bounded by the same 100 ms (CON-SUP-106); the product-owner decisions do not define start-up servicing of the watchdog, so refresh behaviour before control cycles begin, and whether 100 ms from the first cycle is sufficient given the watchdog may already be running, stay open in OP-SYS-004. Gate fix IQ-11.shall-multiple: the second obligation (no refresh after a detected fault until the next reset) is split into SYS-SUP-043.

items.text: The controller shall refresh the window watchdog once per control cycle, at the end of the cycle, only while no alive fault (code 1), late-start fault (code 2), overrun fault (code 3) or flow fault (code 4) has been detected since the last reset.
items.rationale: Finding F-sys-req-item-r2-003: refresh eligibility is defined directly on the detected faults, as in SYS-SUP-010, without attributing a fault to a task. A flow fault (SYS-SUP-006, SYS-SUP-007; CON-SUP-104) is defined for the control cycle, so no per-task health is needed; every detected fault of codes 1 to 4, whichever task or cycle it concerns, stops the refresh. Fault rules: alive (CON-SUP-102), late start and overrun (CON-SUP-103), flow (CON-SUP-104) per SYS-SUP-001, 003, 004, 006, 007. After a fault the recovery path is a reset (CON-SUP-110), so eligibility is evaluated per reset. Refresh behaviour of the window watchdog before the start-up checks pass is not decided by the inputs; see OP-SYS-005. Gate fix IQ-11.shall-multiple: the second obligation (no refresh after a detected fault until the next reset) is split into SYS-SUP-044.

items.text: When an alive fault (code 1), late-start fault (code 2), overrun fault (code 3) or flow fault (code 4) has been detected, the controller shall not refresh the independent watchdog until the next reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-010 (gate IQ-11.shall-multiple); same fault rules. After a fault the recovery path is a reset (CON-SUP-110).

items.text: When an alive fault (code 1), late-start fault (code 2), overrun fault (code 3) or flow fault (code 4) has been detected, the controller shall not refresh the window watchdog until the next reset.
items.rationale: Split from SYS-SUP-011 (gate IQ-11.shall-multiple); same fault rules. After a fault the recovery path is a reset (CON-SUP-110).

items.text: When the window watchdog is refreshed earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after its previous refresh, the controller shall perform a hardware reset.
When the independent watchdog has not been refreshed for 100 ms, the controller shall perform a hardware reset.
At start-up, before any task is released, the controller shall check the integrity of the application image in flash between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end (at most 1 MiB).
items.rationale: CON-SUP-107 defines the image extent but no check algorithm or reference value for the application image (its stored CRC-32 applies to the configuration block only); the method is not specified here, see OP-SYS-006.

items.text: When the start-up check of the application image fails, the controller shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up (code 5).
At start-up, before any task is released, the controller shall check the configuration block against its stored CRC-32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7).
items.rationale: CON-SUP-107 gives only the polynomial; initial value, reflection, final XOR and the byte range covered by the stored CRC are not in the inputs and are not invented here. Recorded as blocking OP-SYS-007; the requirement is not fully verifiable until it is resolved.

items.text: When the start-up check of the configuration block fails, the controller shall detect a configuration integrity fault (code 6).
During normal operation, the controller shall check one 1 KiB segment of the application image per control cycle.
The controller shall complete a full run-time check pass of a 1 MiB application image within 11 s.
The controller shall use at most 0.5 ms of processor time per control cycle for the run-time code check.
When a run-time code check detects a mismatch, the controller shall detect a run-time code integrity fault (code 7).
When a fault is detected, the controller shall switch both control outputs off (driven low) within 50 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
When a fault is detected, the controller shall drive the status signal low (not operational) within 50 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
From any reset until the start-up checks have passed, the controller shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low.
While the start-up checks have passed, no fault is present and the safe-state latch is not set, the controller shall drive the status signal high (operational).
items.rationale: Operational state must be signalled for the low level to be meaningful; implied by the polarity in CON-SUP-109. The safe-state latch condition follows from CON-SUP-110 (latch kept until power-on, across software and watchdog resets) and SYS-SUP-027/SYS-SUP-028.

items.text: The controller shall complete the transmission of the fault report on the diagnostic line before it requests a software reset.
items.rationale: The 20 ms in CON-SUP-110 bounds the reset request (SYS-SUP-042), not the transmission; the 10 ms transmission deadline is SYS-SUP-032 (CON-SUP-112). This item keeps only the ordering of report before reset, so it states no deadline that conflicts with SYS-SUP-032 or SYS-SUP-022/023. Whether the report must also follow safe-state entry is open: OP-SYS-008.

items.text: When the same fault code has caused 3 consecutive supervisor resets without 60 s of fault-free operation in between, the controller shall remain in the safe state until a power-on reset.
The controller shall keep the safe-state latch and the fault history across software and watchdog resets.
At start-up, the controller shall classify the reset cause from the reset flags as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor (software) reset, or other.
At start-up, the controller shall send the reset cause in a start-up message on the diagnostic line.
When the reset cause is an independent watchdog or window watchdog reset, the controller shall detect a watchdog reset fault (code 8).
items.rationale: Item text unchanged: the intended reporting and recovery behaviour for a watchdog reset is not decided in the inputs and must not be invented here. The interaction with the fault reaction (SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-023, SYS-SUP-027, SYS-SUP-042) and the entity value for code 8 are recorded in blocking open point OP-SYS-009; the item is to be completed after the product owner decides.

items.text: Within 10 ms of detecting a fault, the controller shall send on the diagnostic line the line FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed, with the fault code 1 to 9 and the task name, CODE or CONFIG as entity.
The controller shall operate the diagnostic line at 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.
When the request GET STATUS is received on the diagnostic line, the controller shall answer STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms.
items.rationale: Finding F-sys-req-item-r1-011 asks for the permitted <state> values; neither CON-SUP-113 nor any other input defines them, so they are not invented here. The gap is recorded as blocking open point OP-SYS-010.

items.text: When the request GET FAULTS is received on the diagnostic line while at least 8 fault reports are retained, the controller shall answer the last 8 fault reports within 50 ms.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-113 specifies the answer only as the last 8 fault reports. The response for fewer than 8 retained reports, including an empty history, is not in the inputs and is not invented here; it is recorded as blocking OP-SYS-011, and this item is limited to the case where at least 8 are retained.

items.text: When any other request is received on the diagnostic line, the controller shall answer ERR.
In normal operation (no fault, no service request), the supervisor shall use at most 10 % of processor time over any 1 s window, measured on the simulator at the configured core clock.
The controller shall allow injection of each fault class (codes 1 to 9) through test hooks that exist only in test builds.
The supervisor shall execute on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform descriptions, without real hardware, for integration and system tests.
The supervisor shall supervise the 10 ms tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT, released in that order every 10 ms, and the 100 ms task T_DIAG, released after T_OUT in every tenth 10 ms period.
The supervisor shall be implemented in C11 without dynamic memory allocation and without recursion.
items.rationale: Platform constraint CON-SUP-004 applies to the whole software; no stakeholder need states it.

items.text: After entering the safe state and transmitting the fault report, the controller shall request a software reset within 20 ms of entering the safe state, except when the safe state is latched until power-on, that is, when the entered safe state is the latch of SYS-SUP-027 (3 consecutive supervisor resets with the same fault code without 60 s of fault-free operation in between) or the latch caused by a configuration fault (code 9) at start-up.
items.rationale: Finding F-sys-req-item-r1-013: reset is conditional. STK-SUP-010 and CON-SUP-110 keep the safe state until power-on once the repeated-fault latch applies (SYS-SUP-027), and CON-SUP-115 latches the safe state on a configuration fault (code 9, SYS-SUP-009). The latch applies after 3 supervisor resets with the same code, so the reset request is made for the first 3 occurrences; this follows the wording of CON-SUP-110 and is not a new decision.

items.text: The controller shall make the classified reset cause of the latest start-up readable by the service tool on the diagnostic line.
items.rationale: Finding F-sys-req-set-r1-010: CON-SUP-111 requires the cause to be readable by the service tool. CON-SUP-113 lists only GET STATUS, GET FAULTS and ERR for other requests and defines no request or answer for the reset cause; the request syntax and answer format are not invented here, see blocking OP-SYS-013.

items.text: When a configuration fault (code 9) is detected at start-up, the controller shall set the safe-state latch, which remains set until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: Finding F-sys-req-set-r1-011: CON-SUP-115 states the configuration fault latches the safe state; this is the latch referred to in SYS-SUP-042. Persistence across software and watchdog resets follows CON-SUP-110 and SYS-SUP-028.

open_points.text: CON-SUP-112 defines the time stamp as 'ms since start' without saying whether it counts from the last reset or from power-on; the reference instant is needed to make SYS-SUP-032 fully verifiable.

CON-SUP-103 defines an overrun as an execution 'longer than the limit' detected 'when the limit expires'. The product owner must decide the boundary case: whether a task that completes exactly at the instant its execution time equals the limit is an overrun (SYS-SUP-004).

CON-SUP-104 requires the checkpoints of all tasks released in a control cycle to arrive by the end of that cycle, while CON-SUP-103 permits T_DIAG to execute for up to 20 ms, longer than the 10 ms cycle. The product owner must decide the flow-check rule for T_DIAG (for example the position of its checkpoint within execution, and the cycle in which it is due). Until then no requirement covers the flow check of T_DIAG; SYS-SUP-007 covers T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT only. SYS-SUP-006 (not part of this rework) uses the same cycle-end rule for all released tasks and is affected by the same decision.

The inputs do not say whether the independent watchdog is refreshed while the start-up integrity checks (CON-SUP-107, up to 1 MiB CRC) are running, before alive supervision starts (CON-SUP-102), nor how the 100 ms timeout (CON-SUP-106) is met during that phase. The product owner must decide the refresh rule for the start-up phase (SYS-SUP-010).

As for the independent watchdog in OP-SYS-004, the inputs do not say whether or how the window watchdog (CON-SUP-106, one refresh per control cycle, window 6 ms to 12 ms) is refreshed before the start-up integrity checks (CON-SUP-107) have passed and control cycles begin. The product owner must decide the window watchdog refresh rule for the start-up phase (SYS-SUP-011).

CON-SUP-107 gives a stored CRC-32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7) only for the configuration block. The inputs do not specify the integrity method for the application image (algorithm, where the reference value is held, how it is produced) nor the failure reaction. The product owner must decide the application-image integrity method and reference data (SYS-SUP-014); the requirement then needs the method added and the failure reaction confirmed.

CON-SUP-107 gives only the CRC-32 polynomial 0x04C11DB7 and says the configuration data is one block with its own stored CRC-32. The inputs do not give the initial value, input and output reflection, final XOR, the byte range covered by the CRC (whole block or excluding the stored CRC field), the location and byte order of the stored CRC, or a reference check value. The product owner must supply a complete CRC definition so SYS-SUP-016 has a unique expected result.

CON-SUP-112 requires the fault report within 10 ms of detection (SYS-SUP-032), while CON-SUP-110 says the report is transmitted after entering the safe state, and SYS-SUP-022/SYS-SUP-023 allow up to 50 ms from detectability to switch outputs off. The inputs do not say whether the report may precede safe-state entry, nor whether safe-state entry must be reached within 10 ms of detection. The product owner must decide the order and deadlines (SYS-SUP-026, SYS-SUP-032, SYS-SUP-042).

The inputs do not say how a watchdog reset (CON-SUP-111, code 8 of CON-SUP-112) interacts with the fault reaction. If it is treated as a detected fault, SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-023, SYS-SUP-042 and SYS-SUP-027 apply, so the controller enters the safe state and requests a supervisor reset after every watchdog reset; it is not stated whether that is intended, whether code 8 is only reported at start-up (SYS-SUP-030) without a safe-state reaction, or whether the safe state is entered only when the watchdog reset repeats. Also missing: the entity value to report for code 8 (CON-SUP-112 allows only a task name, CODE or CONFIG). The product owner must decide the reporting and recovery behaviour for a watchdog reset (SYS-SUP-031).

CON-SUP-113 returns STS,<state>,<fault count> but no input defines the permitted values of <state>, their spelling or their mapping to controller states. The product owner must supply the value set and mapping so SYS-SUP-034 is verifiable.

CON-SUP-106 gives the independent watchdog timeout (100 ms) but no refresh period or timing margin for fault-free operation (for example once per control cycle). SYS-SUP-010 therefore only requires an interval below 100 ms. The product owner must decide the refresh period or the maximum interval, with a margin, if a tighter rule is wanted.

CON-SUP-113 says GET FAULTS returns the last 8 fault reports but not the response when fewer than 8 reports are retained, including an empty history (whether only the retained reports are returned, whether the answer is padded, whether an end marker or an empty answer is sent, and the line format). The product owner must define this response so SYS-SUP-035 can be extended to cover it.

CON-SUP-111 says the reset cause is readable by the service tool, but CON-SUP-113 defines no request or answer for it, and SYS-SUP-036 answers any other request with ERR. The product owner must decide how the service tool reads the cause (a new request and answer format, or an addition to the GET STATUS answer) so SYS-SUP-045 is verifiable.
